labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE (de-bridged): VICE runs on the host, headless, no QEMU/QMP, no guest OS, no X, no exec channel. Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/plus4/sta/golden.vsf.

museum.blurb: Commodore’s misfire, and the reason it is worth looking at: an office suite — word processor, spreadsheet, database, graphing — burned into ROM and running one second after you switch the machine on, with no disk in sight.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (xplus4) emulating a PAL Plus/4; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the Commodore ROMs INCLUDING both 3-plus-1 banks, so this tile needs no external media. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen, whose ROM message “3-PLUS-1 ON KEY F1” is the exhibit's launcher. The suite’s command prompt is one-shot — C= + C opens it, one command runs, it closes — so module switching needs the Commodore key (Tab under VICE’s symbolic keymap); the SPA’s plus4 on-screen keyboard therefore carries one-tap Word/Calc/File buttons that send the whole sequence. Keyboard-only exhibit; beige-tower-crt fallback archetype. See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/plus4.md.

reset.fixture: Commodore Plus/4 (PAL) power-on screen (BASIC V3.5, 60671 bytes free, “3-PLUS-1 ON KEY F1”), HOST-NATIVE: VICE 3.10.0's xplus4 runs on the host, headless, and publishes the emulated screen straight into the shm mapping at 768x576 (-TEDdsize, -TEDborders 0). resetMode=relaunch, and this station COLD-BOOTS: the launcher restarts xplus4 with VICE_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT=0 and no checkpoint is restored, because a restored Plus/4 snapshot CRASHES INTO TEDMON a few seconds later (BREAK plus a register dump at PC=$0005, and a shorter TED paper area). Measured 2026-08-16 on both a station-baked and a rig-baked checkpoint, so it is the restore and not the bake; a cold boot of the same binary is stable to 120 M cycles. The exhibit loses nothing, because the scene IS an untouched cold boot — the checkpoint only ever bought the ~2 s the ROM takes to reach READY. An earlier bridge-era golden curated INSIDE the 3-plus-1 suite was replaced for the reason that still holds: a visitor arriving mid-application has no idea what it is or how to leave, and the machine's own screen is both its honest empty state and a better launcher than anything the gallery could invent. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); TED sound -> FIFO.
